      physicalExponent (paperOrbitExponent n) / heightC z *
        fixedPhaseGreenScale n z:=

declarations.name: fixedPhaseGreenScale_succ
declarations.header:
theorem fixedPhaseGreenScale_succ (n : ℤ) (z : ℍ) :
    ((weightFiberScale (-paperOrbitExponent (n + 1)) z : ℝ) : ℂ) =
      heightC z ^ 2 * fixedPhaseGreenScale n z:=

declarations.name: dx_fixedPhaseGreenScalarDensity
declarations.header:
theorem dx_fixedPhaseGreenScalarDensity (n : ℤ)
    (u : InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore n)
    (v : InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore (n + 1)) (z : ℍ) :
    dx (fixedPhaseGreenScalarDensity n u v) z =
      fixedPhaseGreenScale n z *
        (star (dx
            (((u : SmoothQuotientCompactFunction) : ℍ → ℂ)) z) *
            (v : SmoothQuotientCompactFunction) z +
          star ((u : SmoothQuotientCompactFunction) z) *
            dx (((v : SmoothQuotientCompactFunction) : ℍ → ℂ)) z):=

declarations.name: dy_fixedPhaseGreenScalarDensity
declarations.header:
theorem dy_fixedPhaseGreenScalarDensity (n : ℤ)
    (u : InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore n)
    (v : InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore (n + 1)) (z : ℍ) :
    dy (fixedPhaseGreenScalarDensity n u v) z =
      physicalExponent (paperOrbitExponent n) / heightC z *
          fixedPhaseGreenScalarDensity n u v z +
        fixedPhaseGreenScale n z *
          (star (dy
              (((u : SmoothQuotientCompactFunction) : ℍ → ℂ)) z) *
              (v : SmoothQuotientCompactFunction) z +
            star ((u : SmoothQuotientCompactFunction) z) *
              dy (((v : SmoothQuotientCompactFunction) : ℍ → ℂ)) z):=

declarations.name: fixedPhaseGreenScalarDensity_realSmooth
declarations.header:
theorem fixedPhaseGreenScalarDensity_realSmooth (n : ℤ)
    (u : InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore n)
    (v : InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore (n + 1)) :
    SmoothCompactCoreGeometry.RealSmooth (fixedPhaseGreenScalarDensity n u v):=

declarations.name: fixedPhaseGreenFlux_divergence_eq_normalizedBulk
declarations.header:
theorem fixedPhaseGreenFlux_divergence_eq_normalizedBulk (n : ℤ)
    (u : InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore n)
    (v : InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore (n + 1)) (z : ℍ) :
    dx (fixedPhaseGreenFluxX n u v) z +
        dy (fixedPhaseGreenFluxY n u v) z =
      fixedPhaseGreenScale n z *
        (star
            (raiseRaw (paperOrbitExponent n)
              (((u : SmoothQuotientCompactFunction) : ℍ → ℂ)) z) *
            (v : SmoothQuotientCompactFunction) z +
          star ((u : SmoothQuotientCompactFunction) z) *
            (lowerRaw (paperOrbitExponent n + 4)
              (((v : SmoothQuotientCompactFunction) : ℍ → ℂ)) z /
                heightC z ^ 2)):=

declarations.name: heightSq_mul_fixedPhaseGreenFlux_divergence
declarations.header:
theorem heightSq_mul_fixedPhaseGreenFlux_divergence (n : ℤ)
    (u : InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore n)
    (v : InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore (n + 1)) (z : ℍ) :
    heightC z ^ 2 *
        (dx (fixedPhaseGreenFluxX n u v) z +
          dy (fixedPhaseGreenFluxY n u v) z) =
      upstairsInnerDensity (OrbitMultiplier (n + 1))
          (InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore.toSmoothCompactWeightCore (n + 1)
            (InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore.raise n u))
          (InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore.toSmoothCompactWeightCore (n + 1) v) z +
        upstairsInnerDensity (OrbitMultiplier n)
          (InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore.toSmoothCompactWeightCore n u)
          (InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore.toSmoothCompactWeightCore n
            (InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore.lowerFromSucc n v)) z:=

declarations.name: fixedPhaseGreenFlux_divergence_integrableOn
declarations.header:
theorem fixedPhaseGreenFlux_divergence_integrableOn (n : ℤ)
    (u : InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore n)
    (v : InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore (n + 1)) :
    IntegrableOn
      (fun z => heightC z ^ 2 *
        (dx (fixedPhaseGreenFluxX n u v) z +
          dy (fixedPhaseGreenFluxY n u v) z))

declarations.name: greenBoundaryDefect_eq_integral_fixedPhaseGreenFlux
declarations.header:
theorem greenBoundaryDefect_eq_integral_fixedPhaseGreenFlux (n : ℤ)
    (u : InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore n)
    (v : InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore (n + 1)) :
    greenBoundaryDefect n u v =
      ∫ z in chosenGammaTwoFundamentalDomain.carrier,

          (dx (fixedPhaseGreenFluxX n u v) z +
            dy (fixedPhaseGreenFluxY n u v) z)

declarations.name: fixedPhaseGreen_fluxOneFormValue
declarations.header:

        (fixedPhaseGreenFluxX n u v) (fixedPhaseGreenFluxY n u v)

/-- Specialization of the pullback law to every edge of the actual measured
six-tile polygon carrier. -/

declarations.name: fixedPhaseGreenFlux_actualPolygonEdge_pairing
declarations.header:
theorem fixedPhaseGreenFlux_actualPolygonEdge_pairing (n : ℤ)

    (v : InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore (n + 1))

        (fixedPhaseGreenFluxX n u v) (fixedPhaseGreenFluxY n u v)

          (gammaTwoActualPolygonEdgeParam e t) ξ) =
      fluxOneFormValue
        (fixedPhaseGreenFluxX n u v) (fixedPhaseGreenFluxY n u v)
        (gammaTwoActualPolygonEdgeParam e t) ξ :=

    (fixedPhaseGreenFlux_invariant n u v) e t ξ

/-- Exact, non-circular packaging of the concrete bridge from the fixed-phase
defect to compact-flux Stokes.  Its equality identifies the defect with the
integral of the explicitly displayed divergence; it does not assume that
either side vanishes. -/
def FixedPhaseGreenFluxBridgeStatement : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℤ) (u : InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore n)
      (v : InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore (n + 1)),
    IsSmoothQuotientCompactFlux
        (fixedPhaseGreenFluxX n u v) (fixedPhaseGreenFluxY n u v) ∧
      IntegrableOn
        (fun z => heightC z ^ 2 *
          (dx (fixedPhaseGreenFluxX n u v) z +
            dy (fixedPhaseGreenFluxY n u v) z))
        chosenGammaTwoFundamentalDomain.carrier hyperbolicMeasure ∧
      greenBoundaryDefect n u v =
        ∫ z in chosenGammaTwoFundamentalDomain.carrier,
          heightC z ^ 2 *
            (dx (fixedPhaseGreenFluxX n u v) z +
              dy (fixedPhaseGreenFluxY n u v) z)
            ∂hyperbolicMeasure

smoothness, quotient-compact support, side-pairing covariance, integrability,
and the exact identification of the Petersson defect with its divergence

compact-core Green identity.  Thus the remaining analytic obligation is
isolated without being postulated. -/

declarations.name: greenBoundaryDefect_eq_zero_iff
declarations.header:
theorem greenBoundaryDefect_eq_zero_iff (n : ℤ)
    (u : InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore n)
    (v : InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore (n + 1)) :
    greenBoundaryDefect n u v = 0 ↔
      peterssonForm (OrbitMultiplier (n + 1))
          chosenGammaTwoFundamentalDomain
          (InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore.toSmoothCompactWeightCore (n + 1)
            (InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore.raise n u))
          (InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore.toSmoothCompactWeightCore (n + 1) v) =
        -peterssonForm (OrbitMultiplier n)
          chosenGammaTwoFundamentalDomain
          (InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore.toSmoothCompactWeightCore n u)
          (InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore.toSmoothCompactWeightCore n
            (InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore.lowerFromSucc n v)):=

/-! ### A concrete nonzero bounded cusp-decaying potential

The modular discriminant supplies an actual potential rather than a potential
certificate.  We use its Petersson self-density

`VΔ(z) = ‖conj(Δ z) * Δ z * Im(z)^12‖`.

It is strictly positive, continuous, invariant under the full modular group
(hence under `Gamma(2)`), uniformly bounded, and tends to zero exponentially
at every cusp after applying any integral scaling matrix.  It therefore
descends to the effective quotient.  On every shifted-weight compact core the
associated Hermitian potential form is genuinely integrable and its diagonal
has an explicit relative Petersson bound.  Since `VΔ ≥ 0`, its negative part
vanishes identically.The pointwise decay is connected below to the literal geometric three-cusp
truncations.  The final `H¹ → H⁻¹` compactness step still requires a local
Rellich theorem on those compact stages; no compactness claim is hidden here.
-/

    (a : ℤ) (z : ℍ) :
    raiseRaw a (χ * f) z =
      χ z * raiseRaw a f z +

/-- Real downstairs shell supported where

    (q : GammaTwoQuotient) : ℝ :=
  expNegInvGlue (potential q - potentialShellLevel N / 2) *
    expNegInvGlue (2 * potentialShellLevel N - potential q)

    expNegInvGlue

declarations.name: localizeStar_euclideanRaiseGauge
declarations.header:
theorem localizeStar_euclideanRaiseGauge (n : ℤ)
    (f : ℍ → ℂ) (hf : RealSmooth f) (v : AmbientTestCore) :
    HalfWeightCompactCoordinateGreen.localizeLeft
        (fun z => star (euclideanRaiseGauge n f z))
        (RealSmooth.conj (euclideanRaiseGauge_realSmooth n hf)) v =
      (-Complex.I) •
          HalfWeightCompactCoordinateGreen.localizeLeft
            (dx (fun z => star (f z)))
            (RealSmooth.dx (RealSmooth.conj hf))
            (HalfWeightCompactCoordinateGreen.rpowMul 1 v) +
        HalfWeightCompactCoordinateGreen.localizeLeft
          (dy (fun z => star (f z)))
          (RealSmooth.dy (RealSmooth.conj hf))
          (HalfWeightCompactCoordinateGreen.rpowMul 1 v) +
        ((euclideanGaugeExponent n + 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) •
          HalfWeightCompactCoordinateGreen.localizeLeft
            (fun z => star (f z)) (RealSmooth.conj hf) v:=

        (fun z => star (euclideanLowerFromSuccGauge n f z))
        (RealSmooth.conj (euclideanLowerFromSuccGauge_realSmooth n hf)) v =
      Complex.I •
          HalfWeightCompactCoordinateGreen.localizeLeft
            (dx (fun z => star (f z)))
            (RealSmooth.dx (RealSmooth.conj hf))
            (HalfWeightCompactCoordinateGreen.rpowMul 1 v) +
        HalfWeightCompactCoordinateGreen.localizeLeft
          (dy (fun z => star (f z)))
          (RealSmooth.dy (RealSmooth.conj hf))
          (HalfWeightCompactCoordinateGreen.rpowMul 1 v) -
        ((euclideanGaugeExponent n + 1 : ℝ) : ℂ) •
          HalfWeightCompactCoordinateGreen.localizeLeft
            (fun z => star (f z)) (RealSmooth.conj hf) v:=

/-!
### P2.4 follow-up: nonzero fixed-phase cores at every orbit index

The orbit-zero inverse-eta seed is not raised or lowered to obtain the
examples below: a differential operator can kill a nonzero vector.  Instead
we differentiate a genuinely nonconstant invariant scalar.  Its two
Wirtinger directions give integral-weight factors of weights `2` and `-2`.
Their ordinary powers change the inverse-eta factor by exactly `j^(2*n)` at
every `n : ℤ`.  Finally a discriminant cutoff whose level is chosen at a
proved nonvanishing point supplies quotient-compact support.
-/

namespace Mock2FA
namespace PaperCorrections
namespace AutomorphicSobolev
namespace ExplicitDiscriminantPotential

open Set Function Topology
open GammaTwoQuotientGeometry
open HalfIntegralMultiplier SmoothCompactCoreGeometry
open HalfWeightDifferentialOperators
open MeasureTheory
open scoped ContDiff

/-! #### A nonzero invariant differential generator -/

/-- The discriminant cutoff vanishes at some honest upper-half-plane point.
This is a consequence of its proved cusp decay, not an added witness. -/

declarations.name: exists_upstairsCoreCutoff_eq_zero
declarations.header:
theorem exists_upstairsCoreCutoff_eq_zero :
    ∃ z : ℍ, upstairsCoreCutoff z = 0:=

declarations.name: exists_fderiv_upstairsCoreCutoff_ne_zero
declarations.header:
theorem exists_fderiv_upstairsCoreCutoff_ne_zero :
    ∃ z : ℍ,
      fderiv ℝ (upperLift upstairsCoreCutoff) (z : ℂ) ≠ 0:=

declarations.name: fixedPhaseHolomorphicDirection_realSmooth
declarations.header:
theorem fixedPhaseHolomorphicDirection_realSmooth :
    RealSmooth fixedPhaseHolomorphicDirection:=

declarations.name: fixedPhaseAntiholomorphicDirection_realSmooth
declarations.header:
theorem fixedPhaseAntiholomorphicDirection_realSmooth :
    RealSmooth fixedPhaseAntiholomorphicDirection:=

declarations.name: fderiv_upstairsCoreCutoff_eq_zero_of_directions_eq_zero
declarations.header:
theorem fderiv_upstairsCoreCutoff_eq_zero_of_directions_eq_zero
    (z : ℍ)
    (hHol : fixedPhaseHolomorphicDirection z = 0)
    (hAnti : fixedPhaseAntiholomorphicDirection z = 0) :
    fderiv ℝ (upperLift upstairsCoreCutoff) (z : ℂ) = 0:=

declarations.name: exists_fixedPhase_direction_ne_zero
declarations.header:
theorem exists_fixedPhase_direction_ne_zero :
    ∃ z : ℍ,
      fixedPhaseHolomorphicDirection z ≠ 0 ∨
        fixedPhaseAntiholomorphicDirection z ≠ 0:=

declarations.name: realSmooth_conj_comp
declarations.header:
theorem realSmooth_conj_comp {f : ℍ → ℂ} (hf : RealSmooth f) :
    RealSmooth (fun z ↦ star (f z)) :=
  RealSmooth.conj hf

/-- The holomorphic direction has exact integral weight `+2`. -/

declarations.name: fixedPhaseHolomorphicDirection_covariance
declarations.header:
theorem fixedPhaseHolomorphicDirection_covariance
    (γ : GammaTwo) (z : ℍ) :
    fixedPhaseHolomorphicDirection
        (((γ : GammaTwo) : SL(2, ℤ)) • z) =
      inverseEtaPaperOrbitDenom γ z ^ (2 : ℕ) *
        fixedPhaseHolomorphicDirection z:=

declarations.name: fixedPhaseAntiholomorphicDirection_covariance
declarations.header:
theorem fixedPhaseAntiholomorphicDirection_covariance
    (γ : GammaTwo) (z : ℍ) :
    fixedPhaseAntiholomorphicDirection
        (((γ : GammaTwo) : SL(2, ℤ)) • z) =
      star (inverseEtaPaperOrbitDenom γ z ^ (2 : ℕ)) *
        fixedPhaseAntiholomorphicDirection z:=

declarations.name: exists_fixedPhasePositiveWeightGenerator_ne_zero
declarations.header:

    ∃ z : ℍ, fixedPhasePositiveWeightGenerator z ≠ 0:=

declarations.name: fixedPhasePositiveWeightGenerator_at_point_ne_zero
declarations.header:
theorem fixedPhasePositiveWeightGenerator_at_point_ne_zero :
    fixedPhasePositiveWeightGenerator fixedPhaseGeneratorPoint ≠ 0 :=
  Classical.choose_spec exists_fixedPhasePositiveWeightGenerator_ne_zero

/-- The canonical weight `-2` generator obtained from the positive one by the
Petersson metric. -/
noncomputable def fixedPhaseNegativeWeightGenerator (z : ℍ) : ℂ :=
  heightC z ^ (2 : ℕ) *
    star (fixedPhasePositiveWeightGenerator z)

declarations.name: fixedPhaseNegativeWeightGenerator_realSmooth

/-! ## P2.6: unconditional graph closure and double adjoints

This final operator layer deliberately separates two statements which need
different analysis.  Local compact-test distributional uniqueness proves
closability, hence identifies the double Hilbert adjoint with the canonical
graph closure.  It does **not** identify raising with the adjoint of signed
lowering; that cross-adjoint assertion remains in the earlier Green/Stokes
layer with its explicit hypotheses.
-/

/-! ### Exact reindexing of the actual lowering coordinate -/

/-- The actual lowering map at source index `n+1`, transported only across
the arithmetic identity `(n+1)-1=n`.  This definition exposes the transport
instead of silently conflating the source and target indices. -/
noncomputable def reindexedActualLower (n : ℤ) :
    InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore (n + 1) →ₗ[ℂ]
      InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore n :=
  InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore.lowerFromSucc n

`lowerFromSucc`; both have the same raw differential expression and stable-core
proof. -/

  (l2Coordinate n).comp (reindexedActualLower n)

/-! ### Exact compatibility with the physical closed joint graph -/

/-- Remove the outer `WithLp 2` wrapper from a successor graph vector.  This
is a continuous linear equivalence, so it transports closures exactly. -/
noncomputable def successorGraphUnwrap (n : ℤ) :
    DefinitionOneSobolev.EnergyTarget
        (OrbitPeterssonHilbert (n + 1))
        (OrbitPeterssonHilbert ((n + 1) + 1))

gives exactly the graph of the genuine densely-defined physical joint
operator.  The reverse inclusion uses the algebraic equivalence between the
smooth core and its `L²` range, so no graph-density assertion is hidden. -/

        Set (OrbitPeterssonHilbert (n + 1) × PhysicalJointTarget n)):=

/-!
### P3.4a: finite measured decomposition of the selected six-tile carrier

The curvilinear Green theorem is applied tile by tile.  The lemmas below
remove a separate measure-theoretic ambiguity in that reduction: distinct
selected right-coset images of the *open* modular tile are genuinely
disjoint, and the chosen closed/half-open carrier integral is therefore the
finite sum of the six open-tile integrals.  No boundary integral or Stokes
claim is used here.
-/

namespace Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.GammaTwoQuotientGeometry

open MeasureTheory Set

/-- Distinct selected right-coset images of the open modular tile are
disjoint.  The only full-modular elements carrying one interior point of the
standard tile to another are the central elements `±1`, and both belong to
`Gamma(2)`; hence they cannot connect two distinct right cosets. -/

declarations.header:

    Pairwise (fun q₁ q₂ : GammaTwoRightCoset =>

    (∫ z in gammaTwoOpenCarrier, f z ∂hyperbolicMeasure) =
      ∑ q : GammaTwoRightCoset,
        ∫ z in gammaTwoCosetRep q • ModularGroup.fdo,
          f z ∂hyperbolicMeasure:=

          DX (1, (1 - p.2) * modularLowerHeightDeriv p.1))
      p.1:=

declarations.name: hasDerivAt_curvedTilePiolaY_vertical
declarations.header:
theorem hasDerivAt_curvedTilePiolaY_vertical
    (H : ℝ) {X Y : ℝ × ℝ → ℂ}
    {DX DY : (ℝ × ℝ) →L[ℝ] ℂ}
    {p : ℝ × ℝ}
    (hX : HasFDerivAt X DX (curvedTileRectangleMap H p))
    (hY : HasFDerivAt Y DY (curvedTileRectangleMap H p)) :
    HasDerivAt
      (fun t : ℝ => curvedTilePiolaY H X Y (p.1, t))
      (DY (0, curvedTileJacobian H p.1) +
        modularLowerHeightDeriv p.1 *
          X (curvedTileRectangleMap H p) -
        ((1 - p.2) * modularLowerHeightDeriv p.1 : ℝ) *
          DX (0, curvedTileJacobian H p.1))
      p.2:=

curvedTilePiolaY_differentiableAt

declarations.name: fderiv_curvedTilePiola_divergence
declarations.header:
theorem fderiv_curvedTilePiola_divergence
    (H : ℝ) {X Y : ℝ × ℝ → ℂ}
    {DX DY : (ℝ × ℝ) →L[ℝ] ℂ}
    {p : ℝ × ℝ}

    (hX : HasFDerivAt X DX (curvedTileRectangleMap H p))
    (hY : HasFDerivAt Y DY (curvedTileRectangleMap H p)) :
    fderiv ℝ (curvedTilePiolaX H X) p (1, 0) +
        fderiv ℝ (curvedTilePiolaY H X Y) p (0, 1) =
      (curvedTileJacobian H p.1 : ℂ) *

        (j * Yy + hp * X₀ - om * hp * j * Xy) =
      j * (Xx + Yy):=

declarations.name: baseModularTruncationBoundaryFlux_eq

          baseModularCircularFluxIntegrand

        (∫ s in (0 : ℝ)..(H - modularVertexHeight),
          realProdLift U (1 / 2, modularVertexHeight + s)) -
        ∫ s in (0 : ℝ)..(H - modularVertexHeight),
          realProdLift U (-(1 / 2), modularVertexHeight + s):=

declarations.name: selectedCosetDenom_ne_zero
declarations.header:
theorem selectedCosetDenom_ne_zero (q : GammaTwoRightCoset) (z : ℍ) :
    selectedCosetDenom q z ≠ 0 :=
  UpperHalfPlane.denom_ne_zero (selectedCosetGL q) z

/-- Holomorphic coefficient of the Möbius differential. -/
noncomputable def selectedCosetDerivative
    (q : GammaTwoRightCoset) (z : ℍ) : ℂ :=
  1 / selectedCosetDenom q z ^ 2

/-- The lower-left matrix entry, in the complex coefficient field. -/
noncomputable def selectedCosetLowerLeft (q : GammaTwoRightCoset) : ℂ :=
  (((selectedCosetGL q) 1 0 : ℝ) : ℂ)

/-- The real Jacobian used by Mathlib's change-of-variables theorem. -/
noncomputable def selectedCosetJacobian
    (q : GammaTwoRightCoset) (z : ℍ) : ℝ :=
  |(UpperHalfPlane.smulFDeriv (selectedCosetGL q) (z : ℂ)).det|

/-- Mathlib's real Frechet derivative is complex multiplication by the exact
holomorphic coefficient `(c z + d)^(-2)`. -/

declarations.name: selectedCoset_smulFDeriv_apply
declarations.header:
theorem selectedCoset_smulFDeriv_apply
    (q : GammaTwoRightCoset) (z : ℍ) (ξ : ℂ) :
    UpperHalfPlane.smulFDeriv (selectedCosetGL q) (z : ℂ) ξ =
      selectedCosetDerivative q z * ξ:=

in exactly the form which cancels the derivative-of-Jacobian terms in the

d1_comp_selectedCosetAction
declarations.header:
theorem d1_comp_selectedCosetAction
    (q : GammaTwoRightCoset) {f : ℍ → ℂ} (hf : RealSmooth f)
    (z : ℍ) (ξ : ℂ) :
    d1 (fun w => f (selectedCosetAction q w)) z ξ =
      d1 f (selectedCosetAction q z)
        (UpperHalfPlane.smulFDeriv
          (selectedCosetGL q) (z : ℂ) ξ):=

declarations.name: dx_comp_selectedCosetAction
declarations.header:
theorem dx_comp_selectedCosetAction
    (q : GammaTwoRightCoset) {f : ℍ → ℂ} (hf : RealSmooth f)
    (z : ℍ) :
    dx (fun w => f (selectedCosetAction q w)) z =
      selectedCosetA q z * dx f (selectedCosetAction q z) +
        selectedCosetB q z * dy f (selectedCosetAction q z):=

declarations.name: dy_comp_selectedCosetAction
declarations.header:
theorem dy_comp_selectedCosetAction
    (q : GammaTwoRightCoset) {f : ℍ → ℂ} (hf : RealSmooth f)
    (z : ℍ) :
    dy (fun w => f (selectedCosetAction q w)) z =
      -selectedCosetB q z * dx f (selectedCosetAction q z) +
        selectedCosetA q z * dy f (selectedCosetAction q z):=

declarations.name: integral_complexImage_selectedCoset_smul_eq_jacobian
declarations.header:
theorem integral_complexImage_selectedCoset_smul_eq_jacobian

/-!
### P3.7 audit: the exact maximal-adjoint graph approximation theorem

The cutoff exhaustion constructed above acts on vectors which are *already*
in the smooth quotient-compact core.  Its eventual-equality theorem therefore
cannot by itself approximate an arbitrary vector in a maximal-adjoint domain.
The missing analytic input is a Friedrichs/Gaffney approximation theorem:
every maximal weak graph vector must be approximable, simultaneously in its
base and differential coordinates, by vectors in the actual smooth physical
domain.

This block records that requirement without weakening it.  First it proves a
general sequential characterization of an essential graph core in Hilbert
spaces.  It then specializes the characterization to the two concrete
fixed-phase operators.  Thus the remaining theorem is exposed as an explicit
sequence of genuine physical-core graph vectors, rather than being inferred
from closability, ordinary `L²` density, or the cutoff identity on an already
compactly supported vector.
-/

namespace Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev
namespace FixedPhaseEssentialCoreAudit

open Set Function Topology Filter
open scoped LinearPMap
open DefinitionOneSobolev
open DefinitionOneSobolev.FixedPhasePeterssonCoordinates

/-- Sequential graph-core approximation for a concrete extension `A` of
`S`.  Every point of the full graph of `A` is required to be a limit of a
sequence lying in the graph of `S`; both operator coordinates therefore
converge simultaneously. -/
def HasSequentialGraphCore
    {E F : Type*} [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℂ E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [InnerProductSpace ℂ F]
    (S A : E →ₗ.[ℂ] F) : Prop :=
  ∀ p : E × F, p ∈ A.graph →
    ∃ q : ℕ → E × F,
      (∀ j : ℕ, q j ∈ S.graph) ∧
        Filter.Tendsto q Filter.atTop (nhds p)

/-- In Hilbert spaces the sequential formulation is exactly equality of the
closed small graph with the graph of a closed extension.  The extension and
closedness hypotheses are essential: they supply the inclusion from the
closure of the small graph into the large graph. -/

    {S A : E →ₗ.[ℂ] F} (hSA : S ≤ A) (hA : A.IsClosed) :
    IsEssentialGraphCoreFor S A ↔ HasSequentialGraphCore S A:=

/-! #### B. One literal height works in all six selected cusp charts -/

/-- The open part of the standard modular tile above height `H`.  Its
openness is essential: pointwise zero on this set gives local zero and hence
zero coordinate derivatives. -/
def modularOpenHighTail (H : ℝ) : Set ℍ :=
  ModularGroup.fdo ∩ {z : ℍ | H < z.im}

declarations.name: modularOpenHighTail_isOpen
declarations.header:
theorem modularOpenHighTail_isOpen (H : ℝ) :
    IsOpen (modularOpenHighTail H) :=
  ModularGroup.isOpen_fdo.inter
    (isOpen_lt continuous_const UpperHalfPlane.continuous_im)

/-- Literal vanishing outside one three-cusp truncation yields one common
base-tile height for every selected right-coset representative.  The proof
uses the very same coset `q` in the universal height condition defining
`gammaTwoThreeCuspTruncation`; no comparison between different cusp charts
is postulated. -/

declarations.name: HasZeroThreeCuspTail.exists_commonBaseHeight_zero
declarations.header:
theorem HasZeroThreeCuspTail.exists_commonBaseHeight_zero
    {X Y : ℍ → ℂ} (hTail : HasZeroThreeCuspTail X Y) :
    ∃ H : ℝ, 1 < H ∧
      ∀ (q : GammaTwoRightCoset) (z : ℍ),
        z ∈ ModularGroup.fd → H ≤ z.im →
          X (selectedCosetAction q z) = 0 ∧
            Y (selectedCosetAction q z) = 0:=

declarations.name: selectedFields_eventuallyEq_zero_on_modularOpenHighTail
declarations.header:
theorem selectedFields_eventuallyEq_zero_on_modularOpenHighTail

    (hZero : ∀ (q : GammaTwoRightCoset) (z : ℍ),
      z ∈ ModularGroup.fd → H ≤ z.im →
        X (selectedCosetAction q z) = 0 ∧
          Y (selectedCosetAction q z) = 0)
    (q : GammaTwoRightCoset) {z : ℍ}
    (hz : z ∈ modularOpenHighTail H) :
    (fun w : ℍ => X (selectedCosetAction q w)) =ᶠ[nhds z]
        (0 : ℍ → ℂ) ∧
      (fun w : ℍ => Y (selectedCosetAction q w)) =ᶠ[nhds z]
        (0 : ℍ → ℂ):=

/-!
================================================================================
P3.5: actual selected-cusp `L²` traces on the fixed-phase graph core

The trace target below is the literal `L²` space on the fixed parameter
interval `[-1/2,1/2]`.  Its pointwise weight is not guessed from a displayed
power: it is the square root of the already certified Hermitian fiber scale
times the hyperbolic horocycle density `dt / H`.  This avoids reversing the
sign of `paperOrbitExponent` (the multiplier index is its negative).

The smooth-core restriction and its exact compact-tail vanishing are
unconditional.  The graph-norm trace inequality is proved below by a scalar
log-height estimate, exponential substitution, product/complex-coordinate
transport, the genuine selected Möbius Jacobian, and the three concrete
Petersson coordinates.  Thus the extension to the graph completion and its
full strong cusp limit are unconditional; no scalar decay claim is silently
promoted to an `L²` trace theorem.
================================================================================
-/

  fixedPhaseGreenFlux_eventually_selectedHorocycle_integral_eq_zero
    n u v

/-! #### D. The unconditional one-dimensional and operator algebra -/

/-- Compact support plus one-dimensional FTC controls a boundary value by
the derivative on its entire right tail.  This is the precise scalar step
used in a cusp trace proof; it does not by itself assert an `L²` trace bound. -/

declarations.name: compactSupport_norm_le_integral_Ioi_deriv
declarations.header:
theorem compactSupport_norm_le_integral_Ioi_deriv
    {f : ℝ → ℂ} (hf : ContDiff ℝ 1 f)
    (hcompact : HasCompactSupport f) (H : ℝ) :
    ‖f H‖ ≤ ∫ y in Set.Ioi H, ‖deriv f y‖:=

declarations.name: deriv_height_mul_normSq
declarations.header:
theorem deriv_height_mul_normSq
    {f : ℝ → ℂ} (hf : Differentiable ℝ f) (y : ℝ) :
    deriv (fun r : ℝ => r * ‖f r‖ ^ 2) y =
      ‖f y‖ ^ 2 + 2 * y * ⟪f y, deriv f y⟫_ℝ:=

declarations.name: norm_deriv_height_mul_normSq_le
declarations.header:
theorem norm_deriv_height_mul_normSq_le
    {f : ℝ → ℂ} (hf : Differentiable ℝ f) {y : ℝ} (hy : 0 ≤ y) :
    ‖deriv (fun r : ℝ => r * ‖f r‖ ^ 2) y‖ ≤
      2 * ‖f y‖ ^ 2 + y ^ 2 * ‖deriv f y‖ ^ 2:=

declarations.name: compactSupport_height_mul_normSq_le_energy_Ioi
declarations.header:
theorem compactSupport_height_mul_normSq_le_energy_Ioi
    {f : ℝ → ℂ} (hf : ContDiff ℝ 1 f)
    (hcompact : HasCompactSupport f) {H : ℝ} (hH : 1 ≤ H) :
    H * ‖f H‖ ^ 2 ≤
      ∫ y in Set.Ioi H,
        (2 * ‖f y‖ ^ 2 + y ^ 2 * ‖deriv f y‖ ^ 2):=

declarations.name: compactSupport_scalarStrip_trace_le_iteratedEnergy
declarations.header:
theorem compactSupport_scalarStrip_trace_le_iteratedEnergy
    (f : ℝ → ℝ → ℂ) {H : ℝ} (hH : 1 ≤ H)
    (hsmooth : ∀ t, ContDiff ℝ 1 (f t))
    (hcompact : ∀ t, HasCompactSupport (f t))
    (htrace : IntegrableOn (fun t => H * ‖f t H‖ ^ 2)
      (Set.Icc (-(1 / 2 : ℝ)) (1 / 2 : ℝ)))
    (henergy : IntegrableOn (fun t =>
        ∫ y in Set.Ioi H,
          (2 * ‖f t y‖ ^ 2 + y ^ 2 * ‖deriv (f t) y‖ ^ 2))
      (Set.Icc (-(1 / 2 : ℝ)) (1 / 2 : ℝ))) :
    (∫ t in Set.Icc (-(1 / 2 : ℝ)) (1 / 2 : ℝ),
        H * ‖f t H‖ ^ 2) ≤
      ∫ t in Set.Icc (-(1 / 2 : ℝ)) (1 / 2 : ℝ),
        ∫ y in Set.Ioi H,
          (2 * ‖f t y‖ ^ 2 + y ^ 2 * ‖deriv (f t) y‖ ^ 2):=

declarations.name: norm_deriv_normSq_le_energy
declarations.header:
theorem norm_deriv_normSq_le_energy
    {f : ℝ → ℂ} (hf : Differentiable ℝ f) (r : ℝ) :
    ‖deriv (fun s : ℝ => ‖f s‖ ^ 2) r‖ ≤
      ‖f r‖ ^ 2 + ‖deriv f r‖ ^ 2:=

declarations.name: tendsto_zero_normSq_le_energy_Ioi
declarations.header:
theorem tendsto_zero_normSq_le_energy_Ioi
    {f : ℝ → ℂ} (hf : ContDiff ℝ 1 f) {r₀ : ℝ}
    (hzero : Filter.Tendsto f Filter.atTop (nhds 0))
    (henergy : IntegrableOn
      (fun r => ‖f r‖ ^ 2 + ‖deriv f r‖ ^ 2) (Set.Ioi r₀)) :
    ‖f r₀‖ ^ 2 ≤
      ∫ r in Set.Ioi r₀, (‖f r‖ ^ 2 + ‖deriv f r‖ ^ 2):=

declarations.name: eventuallyEq_zero_energy_integrableOn_Ioi
declarations.header:
theorem eventuallyEq_zero_energy_integrableOn_Ioi
    {f : ℝ → ℂ} (hf : ContDiff ℝ 1 f)
    (hzero : f =ᶠ[Filter.atTop] 0) (r₀ : ℝ) :
    IntegrableOn (fun r => ‖f r‖ ^ 2 + ‖deriv f r‖ ^ 2)

declarations.name: dy_eq_half_raiseRaw_add_lowerRaw_div_sub_base
declarations.header:
theorem dy_eq_half_raiseRaw_add_lowerRaw_div_sub_base
    (a : ℤ) (f : ℍ → ℂ) (z : ℍ) :
    dy f z =
      (1 / 2 : ℂ) *
        (raiseRaw a f z + lowerRaw a f z / heightC z ^ 2 -
          physicalExponent a / heightC z * f z):=

declarations.name: norm_dy_le_half_raise_lower_base
declarations.header:
theorem norm_dy_le_half_raise_lower_base
    (a : ℤ) (f : ℍ → ℂ) (z : ℍ) :
    ‖dy f z‖ ≤
      (‖raiseRaw a f z‖ +
        ‖lowerRaw a f z / heightC z ^ 2‖ +
        ‖physicalExponent a / heightC z * f z‖) / 2:=

declarations.name: euclideanGaugeExponent_pred
declarations.header:
theorem euclideanGaugeExponent_pred (n : ℤ) :
    euclideanGaugeExponent (n - 1) =
      euclideanGaugeExponent n - 1:=

declarations.name: euclideanRaiseGauge_add_lowerPredGauge
declarations.header:
theorem euclideanRaiseGauge_add_lowerPredGauge
    (n : ℤ) (f : ℍ → ℂ) (z : ℍ) :
    euclideanRaiseGauge n f z +
        euclideanLowerFromSuccGauge (n - 1) f z =
      2 * heightC z * dy f z + 2 * f z:=

declarations.name: height_mul_dy_eq_half_euclideanRaise_add_lower_sub
declarations.header:
theorem height_mul_dy_eq_half_euclideanRaise_add_lower_sub
    (n : ℤ) (f : ℍ → ℂ) (z : ℍ) :
    heightC z * dy f z =
      (1 / 2 : ℂ) *
        (euclideanRaiseGauge n f z +
          euclideanLowerFromSuccGauge (n - 1) f z) - f z:=

declarations.name: fixedPhaseEuclideanGauge_lower_pred
declarations.header:
theorem fixedPhaseEuclideanGauge_lower_pred
    (n : ℤ) (u : InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore n) (z : ℍ) :
    fixedPhaseEuclideanGauge (n - 1)
        (InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore.lower n u) z =
      euclideanLowerFromSuccGauge (n - 1)
        (fixedPhaseEuclideanGauge n u) z:=

declarations.name: euclideanRaiseGauge_sub_lowerPredGauge
declarations.header:
theorem euclideanRaiseGauge_sub_lowerPredGauge
    (n : ℤ) (f : ℍ → ℂ) (z : ℍ) :
    euclideanRaiseGauge n f z -
        euclideanLowerFromSuccGauge (n - 1) f z =
      2 * Complex.I * heightC z * dx f z +
        ((2 * (euclideanGaugeExponent n + 1) : ℝ) : ℂ) * f z:=

declarations.name: height_mul_dx_eq_negI_half_raise_sub_lower_sub
declarations.header:
theorem height_mul_dx_eq_negI_half_raise_sub_lower_sub
    (n : ℤ) (f : ℍ → ℂ) (z : ℍ) :
    heightC z * dx f z =
      (-Complex.I / 2) *
        (euclideanRaiseGauge n f z -
          euclideanLowerFromSuccGauge (n - 1) f z -
          ((2 * (euclideanGaugeExponent n + 1) : ℝ) : ℂ) * f z):=

declarations.name: euclideanHorizontalDrift_nonneg
declarations.header:
theorem euclideanHorizontalDrift_nonneg (n : ℤ) :
    0 ≤ euclideanHorizontalDrift n := abs_nonneg _

/-- Norm estimate for the vertical logarithmic derivative in terms of the
three graph coordinates. -/

declarations.name: norm_height_mul_dy_le_euclideanGraph
declarations.header:
theorem norm_height_mul_dy_le_euclideanGraph
    (n : ℤ) (f : ℍ → ℂ) (z : ℍ) :
    ‖heightC z * dy f z‖ ≤
      (‖euclideanRaiseGauge n f z‖ +
        ‖euclideanLowerFromSuccGauge (n - 1) f z‖) / 2 + ‖f z‖:=

declarations.name: norm_height_mul_dx_le_euclideanGraph
declarations.header:
theorem norm_height_mul_dx_le_euclideanGraph
    (n : ℤ) (f : ℍ → ℂ) (z : ℍ) :
    ‖heightC z * dx f z‖ ≤
      (‖euclideanRaiseGauge n f z‖ +
        ‖euclideanLowerFromSuccGauge (n - 1) f z‖ +
        euclideanHorizontalDrift n * ‖f z‖) / 2:=

declarations.name: selectedCosetConformalScaleC_realSmooth
declarations.header:
theorem selectedCosetConformalScaleC_realSmooth
    (q : GammaTwoRightCoset) :
    RealSmooth (selectedCosetConformalScaleC q):=

declarations.name: selectedCosetConformalScaleC_eq_inv_normSq_denom
declarations.header:
theorem selectedCosetConformalScaleC_eq_inv_normSq_denom

declarations.header:
theorem dx_selectedCosetConformalScaleC

theorem dy_selectedCosetConformalScaleC

theorem height_mul_dx_selectedCosetConformalScaleC

declarations.header:
theorem height_mul_dy_selectedCosetConformalScaleC

declarations.header:

declarations.header:

    (q : GammaTwoRightCoset) (z : ℍ) :

declarations.header:
theorem norm_selectedCosetB_le_scale
    (q : GammaTwoRightCoset) (z : ℍ) :

declarations.name: selectedCosetUnitaryPullback_realSmooth
declarations.header:
theorem selectedCosetUnitaryPullback_realSmooth
    (q : GammaTwoRightCoset) {f : ℍ → ℂ} (hf : RealSmooth f) :
    RealSmooth (selectedCosetUnitaryPullback q f) :=
  (selectedCosetConformalScaleC_realSmooth q).mul
    (RealSmooth.comp_selectedCosetAction hf q)

/-- Exact horizontal chain/product rule for the unitary pullback. -/

declarations.name: dx_selectedCosetUnitaryPullback
declarations.header:
theorem dx_selectedCosetUnitaryPullback
    (q : GammaTwoRightCoset) {f : ℍ → ℂ} (hf : RealSmooth f)
    (z : ℍ) :
    dx (selectedCosetUnitaryPullback q f) z =
      dx (selectedCosetConformalScaleC q) z *
          f (selectedCosetAction q z) +
        selectedCosetConformalScaleC q z *
          (selectedCosetA q z * dx f (selectedCosetAction q z) +
            selectedCosetB q z * dy f (selectedCosetAction q z)):=

declarations.name: dy_selectedCosetUnitaryPullback
declarations.header:
theorem dy_selectedCosetUnitaryPullback
    (q : GammaTwoRightCoset) {f : ℍ → ℂ} (hf : RealSmooth f)
    (z : ℍ) :
    dy (selectedCosetUnitaryPullback q f) z =
      dy (selectedCosetConformalScaleC q) z *
          f (selectedCosetAction q z) +
        selectedCosetConformalScaleC q z *
          (-selectedCosetB q z * dx f (selectedCosetAction q z) +
            selectedCosetA q z * dy f (selectedCosetAction q z)):=

declarations.name: height_mul_dy_selectedCosetUnitaryPullback
declarations.header:
theorem height_mul_dy_selectedCosetUnitaryPullback
    (q : GammaTwoRightCoset) {f : ℍ → ℂ} (hf : RealSmooth f)
    (z : ℍ) :
    heightC z * dy (selectedCosetUnitaryPullback q f) z =
      (selectedCosetA q z - selectedCosetConformalScaleC q z) *
          f (selectedCosetAction q z) -
        selectedCosetB q z *
          (heightC (selectedCosetAction q z) *
            dx f (selectedCosetAction q z)) +
        selectedCosetA q z *
          (heightC (selectedCosetAction q z) *
            dy f (selectedCosetAction q z)):=

declarations.name: norm_height_mul_dy_selectedCosetUnitaryPullback_le
declarations.header:
theorem norm_height_mul_dy_selectedCosetUnitaryPullback_le
    (q : GammaTwoRightCoset) {f : ℍ → ℂ} (hf : RealSmooth f)
    (z : ℍ) :
    ‖heightC z * dy (selectedCosetUnitaryPullback q f) z‖ ≤
      ‖selectedCosetConformalScaleC q z‖ *
        (2 * ‖f (selectedCosetAction q z)‖ +
          ‖heightC (selectedCosetAction q z) *
            dx f (selectedCosetAction q z)‖ +
          ‖heightC (selectedCosetAction q z) *
            dy f (selectedCosetAction q z)‖):=

declarations.name: norm_height_mul_dy_selectedCosetUnitaryPullback_le_graph
declarations.header:
theorem norm_height_mul_dy_selectedCosetUnitaryPullback_le_graph
    (n : ℤ) (q : GammaTwoRightCoset) {f : ℍ → ℂ}
    (hf : RealSmooth f) (z : ℍ) :
    ‖heightC z * dy (selectedCosetUnitaryPullback q f) z‖ ≤
      ‖selectedCosetConformalScaleC q z‖ *
        ((3 + euclideanHorizontalDrift n / 2) *
            ‖f (selectedCosetAction q z)‖ +
          ‖euclideanRaiseGauge n f (selectedCosetAction q z)‖ +
          ‖euclideanLowerFromSuccGauge (n - 1) f
            (selectedCosetAction q z)‖):=

/-- Natural log-height trace gauge.  The factor `exp(r/2)` is the square root
of the horocycle height. -/
noncomputable def selectedLogHeightNaturalGauge
    (n : ℤ) (q : GammaTwoRightCoset) (u : InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore n)
    (t : ℝ) : ℝ → ℂ :=
  fun r => ((Real.exp (r / 2) : ℝ) : ℂ) *
    selectedCosetUnitaryPullback q (fixedPhaseEuclideanGauge n u)
      (logHeightBasePoint t r)

vertical line remains `C-infinity`. -/

declarations.header:

declarations.header:
theorem deriv_selectedLogHeightNaturalGauge
    (n : ℤ) (q : GammaTwoRightCoset) (u : InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore n)
    (t r : ℝ) :
    deriv (selectedLogHeightNaturalGauge n q u t) r =
      ((Real.exp (r / 2) : ℝ) : ℂ) *
        ((1 / 2 : ℂ) *
            selectedCosetUnitaryPullback q (fixedPhaseEuclideanGauge n u)
              (logHeightBasePoint t r) +
          heightC (logHeightBasePoint t r) *
            dy (selectedCosetUnitaryPullback q
              (fixedPhaseEuclideanGauge n u))
              (logHeightBasePoint t r)):=

declarations.name: norm_deriv_selectedLogHeightNaturalGauge_le_graph
declarations.header:
theorem norm_deriv_selectedLogHeightNaturalGauge_le_graph
    (n : ℤ) (q : GammaTwoRightCoset) (u : InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore n)

    ‖deriv (selectedLogHeightNaturalGauge n q u t) r‖ ≤

              (fixedPhaseEuclideanGauge n u)
              (selectedCosetAction q (logHeightBasePoint t r))‖):=

/-- The one-dimensional natural gauge has integrable `H¹` energy on every
tail, with no separate integrability assumption. -/

declarations.name: selectedLogHeightNaturalGauge_energy_integrableOn_Ioi
declarations.header:
theorem selectedLogHeightNaturalGauge_energy_integrableOn_Ioi
    (n : ℤ) (q : GammaTwoRightCoset) (u : InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore n)
    {t : ℝ} (ht : t ∈ Set.Icc (-(1 / 2 : ℝ)) (1 / 2 : ℝ))
    (r₀ : ℝ) :

/-- Compactly supported vectors in the raising maximal graph, before adding
the local weak-domain identification. -/
def RaisingCompactMaximalGraphAt (n : ℤ) :
    Set (OrbitPeterssonHilbert n × OrbitPeterssonHilbert (n + 1)) :=
  {p | p ∈ ((-physicalLowerFromSucc n)†).graph ∧
    HasCompactCarrierSupport n p.1 ∧
      HasCompactCarrierSupport (n + 1) p.2}

/-- Compactly supported vectors in the lowering maximal graph. -/
def LoweringCompactMaximalGraphAt (n : ℤ) :
    Set (OrbitPeterssonHilbert (n + 1) × OrbitPeterssonHilbert n) :=
  {p | p ∈ ((-physicalRaise n)†).graph ∧
    HasCompactCarrierSupport (n + 1) p.1 ∧
      HasCompactCarrierSupport n p.2}

/-- The exact raising class to which finite-chart Friedrichs smoothing and
periodization must apply. -/
def RaisingCompactWeakMaximalGraphAt (n : ℤ) :
    Set (OrbitPeterssonHilbert n × OrbitPeterssonHilbert (n + 1)) :=
  {p | p ∈ RaisingCompactMaximalGraphAt n ∧
    IsEuclideanRaisingWeakGraphAt n p}

/-- The exact lowering class to which finite-chart smoothing must apply. -/
def LoweringCompactWeakMaximalGraphAt (n : ℤ) :
    Set (OrbitPeterssonHilbert (n + 1) × OrbitPeterssonHilbert n) :=
  {p | p ∈ LoweringCompactMaximalGraphAt n ∧
    IsEuclideanLoweringWeakGraphAt n p}

/-!
### P3.12: compact physical graphs and the bounded-commutator cutoff mechanism

There are two logically separate points in a maximal-domain cutoff argument.
First, literal smooth physical graph vectors really do have compact support in
the chosen Euclidean carrier; this follows from quotient-compact support and
the already proved properness of the selected closed carrier.  Second, a
bounded multiplier preserves the graph of a Hilbert adjoint only after its
commutator with the opposite core operator has been identified.  Merely
multiplying both graph coordinates by the same cutoff is not valid.

The results below prove both facts at the exact level needed by P3.7.  The
generic `AdjointCutoffExhaustion` theorem reduces invariant maximal-domain
localization to three checkable analytic estimates: strong convergence of the
two bounded multipliers, strong disappearance of the adjoint commutator, and
compact support of the localized pair.  In particular, it makes explicit why
the pointwise stabilization theorem for an already quotient-compact smooth
core vector does not by itself localize an arbitrary maximal graph vector.
-/

theorem adjoint_graph_mem_of_bounded_cutoff_commutator
    {E F : Type*}
    [NormedAddCommGroup E] [InnerProductSpace ℂ E] [CompleteSpace E]
    [NormedAddCommGroup F] [InnerProductSpace ℂ F] [CompleteSpace F]
    (T : E →ₗ.[ℂ] F) (hT : Dense (T.domain : Set E))
    (U : E →L[ℂ] E) (V : F →L[ℂ] F) (C : E →L[ℂ] F)
    (hDomain : ∀ x : T.domain,
      ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint U (x : E) ∈ T.domain)
    (hCommutator : ∀ x : T.domain,
      ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint V (T x) =
        T ⟨ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint U (x : E), hDomain x⟩ + C x)

        U (T† y) + ContinuousLinearMap.adjoint C (y : F)) ∈
      (T†).graph:=

/-!
### P3.15: exact periodization of compact ambient Friedrichs graph approximants

The weak graph equations in P3.11 are written against genuine ambient
`C_c^infinity` tests, whereas the small physical graphs have the exact
fixed-phase automorphy and quotient-compact support.  The locally finite
Gamma(2) periodization proved above bridges these two descriptions not only
for the base coordinate, but simultaneously for the differentiated graph
coordinate.

This section proves that bridge completely.  Thus a local Friedrichs theorem
only has to produce compact ambient tests whose base and forward Maass
coordinates converge in carrier `L2`; periodization, the multiplier phase,
the weight shift, and passage back through the Petersson isometries then add
no further analytic premise.
-/

namespace Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev
namespace FixedPhaseEssentialCoreRoute

open Set Function Topology Filter MeasureTheory

/-! #### Forward Maass operators on the genuine ambient test core -/

/-- The Euclidean-gauge raising expression bundled as an actual ambient
compact test.  Unlike the previously defined test transpose, this is the
forward graph coordinate used by Friedrichs regularization. -/
noncomputable def euclideanRaiseForwardTest (n : ℤ)
    (v : Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.FixedPhaseClosedOperators.PhysicalLocalL2.AmbientTestCore) :
    Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.FixedPhaseClosedOperators.PhysicalLocalL2.AmbientTestCore :=
  Complex.I • HalfWeightCompactCoordinateGreen.rpowMul 1
      (HalfWeightCompactCoordinateGreen.dx v) +
    HalfWeightCompactCoordinateGreen.rpowMul 1
      (HalfWeightCompactCoordinateGreen.dy v) +
    ((Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.FixedPhaseClosedOperators.PhysicalLocalL2.euclideanGaugeExponent n + 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) • v

/-- The forward lowering expression from the successor gauge, again bundled
in the genuine compact test core. -/
noncomputable def euclideanLowerFromSuccForwardTest (n : ℤ)
    (v : Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.FixedPhaseClosedOperators.PhysicalLocalL2.AmbientTestCore) :
    Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.FixedPhaseClosedOperators.PhysicalLocalL2.AmbientTestCore :=
  (-Complex.I) • HalfWeightCompactCoordinateGreen.rpowMul 1
      (HalfWeightCompactCoordinateGreen.dx v) +
    HalfWeightCompactCoordinateGreen.rpowMul 1
      (HalfWeightCompactCoordinateGreen.dy v) -
    ((Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.FixedPhaseClosedOperators.PhysicalLocalL2.euclideanGaugeExponent n + 1 : ℝ) : ℂ) • v

/-- Forward raising does not enlarge ambient topological support. -/

/-!
### P3.17: the affine Maass commutator and strong `L2` translation

After reduced-chart localization, the Euclidean-gauge Maass coefficients are
not general variable coefficients.  Both forward operators have the form

`P f(w) = w.im * D f(w) + c * f(w)`

with a constant first-order operator `D`.  Translation therefore has one
exact commutator, namely `t.im * D f(w-t)`.  This is the algebraic reason the
Friedrichs error is a zero-mean approximate-identity kernel.  The other
analytic ingredient, strong continuity of translations in planar `L2`, is a
Mathlib theorem and is recorded here in the precise form needed below.
-/

namespace Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev
namespace FixedPhaseAffineFriedrichs

open Set Function Topology Filter MeasureTheory
open scoped Convolution
open FixedPhaseEssentialCoreRoute

/-- Ordinary planar scalar `L2`. -/
noncomputable abbrev AmbientPlaneL2 :=
  MeasureTheory.Lp ℂ 2 (volume : Measure ℂ)

/-- Strong continuity of domain translation at the identity in planar `L2`.
The representative of `DomAddAct.mk t +v f` is `w |-> f (t+w)`. -/

declarations.header:

    ambientAffineMaass sigma c (ambientTranslate t f) w -
        ambientTranslate t (ambientAffineMaass sigma c f) w =

        ambientConstantMaassDerivative sigma f (w - t):=

    euclideanLowerFromSuccForwardTest n v w =
      ambientAffineMaass (-Complex.I)

declarations.name: ambientRaiseAffine_translate_commutator
declarations.header:
theorem ambientRaiseAffine_translate_commutator
    (n : ℤ) (t : ℂ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) (w : ℂ) :
    ambientAffineMaass Complex.I
          ((Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.FixedPhaseClosedOperators.PhysicalLocalL2.euclideanGaugeExponent n + 2 : ℝ) : ℂ)
          (ambientTranslate t f) w -
        ambientTranslate t
          (ambientAffineMaass Complex.I
            ((Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.FixedPhaseClosedOperators.PhysicalLocalL2.euclideanGaugeExponent n + 2 : ℝ) : ℂ) f) w =
      (t.im : ℂ) *
        ambientConstantMaassDerivative Complex.I f (w - t) :=
  ambientAffineMaass_translate_commutator _ _ _ _ _

declarations.header:
theorem ambientLowerAffine_translate_commutator
    (n : ℤ) (t : ℂ) (f : ℂ → ℂ) (w : ℂ) :
    ambientAffineMaass (-Complex.I)
          (-((Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.FixedPhaseClosedOperators.PhysicalLocalL2.euclideanGaugeExponent n + 1 : ℝ) : ℂ))
          (ambientTranslate t f) w -
        ambientTranslate t
          (ambientAffineMaass (-Complex.I)
            (-((Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.FixedPhaseClosedOperators.PhysicalLocalL2.euclideanGaugeExponent n + 1 : ℝ) : ℂ)) f) w =
      (t.im : ℂ) *
        ambientConstantMaassDerivative (-Complex.I) f (w - t) :=
  ambientAffineMaass_translate_commutator _ _ _ _ _

/-!
### P3.18: zero-mean shrinking kernels in planar `L2`

The affine commutator kernel has integral zero, uniformly bounded `L1` norm,
and shrinking support.  The following Hilbert-valued Bochner lemma proves
that every such kernel tends strongly to zero on a fixed `L2` vector.  Its
proof uses only the translation continuity from P3.17 and the elementary
Bochner integral norm estimate; no pointwise representative of the `L2`
vector is selected.
-/

namespace Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev
namespace FixedPhaseAffineFriedrichs

open Set Function Topology Filter MeasureTheory Metric

/-- The zero-mean rewrite which removes the non-small untranslated term. -/

declarations.name: integral_kernel_vadd_eq_integral_kernel_vadd_sub_of_mean_zero
declarations.header:

    (hMean : (∫ t : ℂ, K t) = 0)
    (hTranslate : Integrable
      (fun t : ℂ ↦ K t • (DomAddAct.mk (-t) +ᵥ f)))
    (hError : Integrable
      (fun t : ℂ ↦ K t • (DomAddAct.mk (-t) +ᵥ f - f))) :
    (∫ t : ℂ, K t • (DomAddAct.mk (-t) +ᵥ f)) =
      ∫ t : ℂ, K t • (DomAddAct.mk (-t) +ᵥ f - f):=

      Integrable (fun t : ℂ ↦ ‖K n t‖))
    (hL1 : ∀ n : ℕ, (∫ t : ℂ, ‖K n t‖) ≤ C)
    (hSupport : ∀ n : ℕ, ∀ t : ℂ,
      K n t ≠ 0 → ‖t‖ ≤ r n)
    (hr : Filter.Tendsto r Filter.atTop (nhds 0)) :
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun n : ℕ ↦
        ∫ t : ℂ, K n t • (DomAddAct.mk (-t) +ᵥ f - f))
      Filter.atTop (nhds 0):=

  (-sigma) • fullPlaneHeightMul (fullPlaneDirectionalDerivative 1 v) -
    fullPlaneHeightMul (fullPlaneDirectionalDerivative Complex.I v) +
      (c - 1) • v

        (t.im : ℂ) *
          fderiv ℝ (v : ℂ → ℂ) t Complex.I +
        (c - 1) * v t:=

declarations.name: friedrichsAffineCommutatorKernel_expanded
declarations.header:
theorem friedrichsAffineCommutatorKernel_expanded
    (sigma : ℂ) (j : ℕ) (t : ℂ) :
    friedrichsAffineCommutatorKernel sigma j t =
      sigma * (t.im : ℂ) *
          ((fderiv ℝ (friedrichsMollifierReal j) t 1 : ℝ) : ℂ) +
        (t.im : ℂ) *
          ((fderiv ℝ (friedrichsMollifierReal j) t Complex.I : ℝ) : ℂ) +
        friedrichsMollifier j t:=

    .solvable_iff_mem_orthogonal_adjointKernel f

/-- The compatible forcing subtype for the actual PDE. -/
noncomputable abbrev CompatibleForcing
    (n : ℤ) (t : ℝ) := (weakSchrodingerOperator n t).range

/-- Canonical kernel-orthogonal weak solution. -/
noncomputable def canonicalWeakSolution
    (n : ℤ) (t : ℝ)
    (hcompact : IsCompactOperator (graphPotentialOperator n))
    (f : CompatibleForcing n t) : ActualHOne n :=
  (fredholmData_of_compactPotential n t hcompact).canonicalSolution f

        (canonicalWeakSolution n t hcompact f) = (f : ActualHMinusOne n) :=
  (fredholmData_of_compactPotential n t hcompact).canonicalSolution_spec f

    .canonicalSolution_mem_kernelOrthogonal f

/-- Every weak solution is the canonical solution plus one homogeneous
solution, and every such translate is a solution. -/

declarations.name: weakSchrodinger_solves_iff_canonical_add_kernel
declarations.header:
theorem weakSchrodinger_solves_iff_canonical_add_kernel
    (n : ℤ) (t : ℝ)
    (hcompact : IsCompactOperator (graphPotentialOperator n))
    (f : CompatibleForcing n t) (u : ActualHOne n) :
    weakSchrodingerOperator n t u = (f : ActualHMinusOne n) ↔
      ∃ h : ActualHOne n,
        h ∈ (weakSchrodingerOperator n t).ker ∧
          u = canonicalWeakSolution n t hcompact f + h :=
  (fredholmData_of_compactPotential n t hcompact)
    .solves_iff_canonical_add_kernel f u

/-- The actual reduced inverse norm on the compatible forcing range. -/
noncomputable def reducedInverseNorm

    (f : CompatibleForcing n t) :

/-! ### Closed distributional defects -/

/-- Raising defect against one genuine smooth quotient test.  The inner
products are written with the fixed test in the first slot, making this a
complex-linear continuous functional of `(u,r,l)`.  Its vanishing is the
conjugate of
`⟪r,v⟫ = -⟪u,L v⟫`. -/
noncomputable def raisingDefect (n : ℤ)
    (v : Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.HalfWeightDifferentialOperators.InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore ((n + 1) + 1)) :
    WeakCoordinateAmbient n →L[ℂ] ℂ :=
  ((innerSL ℂ (l2Coordinate ((n + 1) + 1) v)).comp
      (raiseProjection n)) +
    ((innerSL ℂ (lowerFromSuccCoordinate (n + 1) v)).comp
      (baseProjection n))

/-- Lowering defect against one genuine smooth quotient test.  Its
vanishing is the conjugate of
`⟪l,v⟫ = -⟪u,R v⟫`. -/
noncomputable def loweringDefect (n : ℤ)
    (v : Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.HalfWeightDifferentialOperators.InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore n) :
    WeakCoordinateAmbient n →L[ℂ] ℂ :=
  ((innerSL ℂ (l2Coordinate n v)).comp (lowerProjection n)) +
    ((innerSL ℂ (raisedCoordinate n v)).comp (baseProjection n))

@[simp]

declarations.name: raisingDefect_apply
declarations.header:
theorem raisingDefect_apply (n : ℤ)
    (v : Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.HalfWeightDifferentialOperators.InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore ((n + 1) + 1))
    (x : WeakCoordinateAmbient n) :
    raisingDefect n v x =
      inner ℂ (l2Coordinate ((n + 1) + 1) v)
          (raiseProjection n x) +
        inner ℂ (lowerFromSuccCoordinate (n + 1) v)
          (baseProjection n x):=

    loweringDefect n v x =
      inner ℂ (l2Coordinate n v) (lowerProjection n x) +
        inner ℂ (raisedCoordinate n v) (baseProjection n x):=

/-!
## P4.2: simultaneous intrinsic localization of both weak derivatives

The same intrinsic cutoff localizes the base coordinate and both maximal
adjoint coordinates.  The raising and lowering commutator errors use the one
uniform derivative bound proved above.  Hence there is one sequence of
compact-carrier triples, with a common cutoff index, converging in all three
Petersson coordinates at once.
-/

namespace Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev
namespace FixedPhaseIntrinsicJointLocalization

open Set Function Topology Filter MeasureTheory
open scoped LinearPMap
open DefinitionOneSobolev
open DefinitionOneSobolev.FixedPhasePeterssonCoordinates
open FixedPhaseDensity
open FixedPhaseClosedOperators
open FixedPhaseAdjointCutoffCore
open FixedPhaseIntrinsicAdjointCutoff
open IndependentWeightedWeakSobolev

/-- One common intrinsic cutoff applied to a weak base coordinate and its two
maximal weak derivatives, including the exact signed commutator terms. -/
noncomputable def intrinsicJointCutoffTriple
    (j : ℕ) (n : ℤ) (x : WeakCoordinateAmbient n) :
    WeakCoordinateAmbient n :=
  WithLp.toLp 2
    (intrinsicPeterssonCuspCutoff j (n + 1) (baseProjection n x),
      WithLp.toLp 2
        (intrinsicPeterssonCuspCutoff j ((n + 1) + 1)
              (raiseProjection n x) +
            intrinsicRaisePeterssonCommutator j (n + 1)
              (baseProjection n x),
          intrinsicPeterssonCuspCutoff j n (lowerProjection n x) +
            intrinsicLowerFromSuccPeterssonCommutator j n
              (baseProjection n x)))

@[simp]

declarations.name: baseProjection_intrinsicJointCutoffTriple
declarations.header:
theorem baseProjection_intrinsicJointCutoffTriple
    (j : ℕ) (n : ℤ) (x : WeakCoordinateAmbient n) :
    baseProjection n (intrinsicJointCutoffTriple j n x) =
      intrinsicPeterssonCuspCutoff j (n + 1) (baseProjection n x) :=
  rfl

@[simp]

declarations.name: raiseProjection_intrinsicJointCutoffTriple
declarations.header:
theorem raiseProjection_intrinsicJointCutoffTriple
    (j : ℕ) (n : ℤ) (x : WeakCoordinateAmbient n) :
    raiseProjection n (intrinsicJointCutoffTriple j n x) =
      intrinsicPeterssonCuspCutoff j ((n + 1) + 1)
          (raiseProjection n x) +
        intrinsicRaisePeterssonCommutator j (n + 1)
          (baseProjection n x) :=
  rfl

@[simp]

declarations.name: lowerProjection_intrinsicJointCutoffTriple
declarations.header:
theorem lowerProjection_intrinsicJointCutoffTriple
    (j : ℕ) (n : ℤ) (x : WeakCoordinateAmbient n) :
    lowerProjection n (intrinsicJointCutoffTriple j n x) =
      intrinsicPeterssonCuspCutoff j n (lowerProjection n x) +
        intrinsicLowerFromSuccPeterssonCommutator j n
          (baseProjection n x) :=
  rfl

/-- All three coordinates of a localized triple have compact carrier
support. -/
def HasJointCompactCarrierSupport (n : ℤ)
    (x : WeakCoordinateAmbient n) : Prop :=
  HasCompactCarrierSupport (n + 1) (baseProjection n x) ∧
    HasCompactCarrierSupport ((n + 1) + 1) (raiseProjection n x) ∧
      HasCompactCarrierSupport n (lowerProjection n x)

/-- Exact quantitative tail predicate used by the Rellich proof.  It only
asks that the displayed finite Fourier approximants converge in operator
norm; compactness is a conclusion below, not part of this definition. -/
def HasVanishingFiniteModeTail
    (b : HilbertBasis I ℂ E) (modes : ℕ → Finset I)
    (T : H →L[ℂ] E) : Prop :=
  Filter.Tendsto
    (fun N ↦ ‖finiteModeLocalization b (modes N) T - T‖)
    Filter.atTop (nhds 0)

declarations.name: finiteModeLocalization_tendsto

declarations.name: IsPlanarAffineWeakGraph.friedrichs_identity

theorem IsPlanarAffineWeakGraph.friedrichs_identity
    {sigma c : ℂ} {u Pu : AmbientPlaneL2}
    (hWeak : IsPlanarAffineWeakGraph sigma c u Pu)
    (j : ℕ) (w : ℂ) :
    ambientAffineMaass sigma c
        (friedrichsMollifiedRepresentative j u) w =

        ∫ x : ℂ,

declarations.name: IsPlanarAffineWeakGraph.friedrichs_raising_identity
declarations.header:
theorem IsPlanarAffineWeakGraph.friedrichs_raising_identity
    {n : ℤ} {u Ru : AmbientPlaneL2}
    (hWeak : IsPlanarAffineWeakGraph Complex.I
      (((Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.FixedPhaseClosedOperators.PhysicalLocalL2.euclideanGaugeExponent n + 2 : ℝ) : ℂ)) u Ru)

    ambientAffineMaass Complex.I
        (((Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.FixedPhaseClosedOperators.PhysicalLocalL2.euclideanGaugeExponent n + 2 : ℝ) : ℂ))
        (friedrichsMollifiedRepresentative j u) w =
      friedrichsMollifiedRepresentative j Ru w +
        ∫ x : ℂ,
          friedrichsAffineCommutatorKernel Complex.I j (w - x) * u x :=
  hWeak.friedrichs_identity j w

declarations.name: IsPlanarAffineWeakGraph.friedrichs_loweringFromSucc_identity
declarations.header:
theorem IsPlanarAffineWeakGraph.friedrichs_loweringFromSucc_identity
    {n : ℤ} {u Lu : AmbientPlaneL2}
    (hWeak : IsPlanarAffineWeakGraph (-Complex.I)
      (-(((Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.FixedPhaseClosedOperators.PhysicalLocalL2.euclideanGaugeExponent n + 1 : ℝ) : ℂ))) u Lu)

/-!
## P5.2: the actual discriminant cusp scale and hard-truncation endpoint

The discriminant potential already has a proved uniform tail on the quotient
outside the image of the literal three-cusp truncation.  Here we choose one
literal height for the explicit null sequence `1 / (N+1)` and connect compact
stage restrictions to the completed graph potential by bounded
postcomposition and operator-norm closure.

No compactness premise is attached to the scalar potential itself.  The only
remaining local input in the last theorem is compactness of the displayed
hard stage restriction; `P5LocalFourierRellich` is designed to prove exactly
that input chart by chart.
-/

namespace Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev
namespace P5DiscriminantHardTruncation

open Function Set Topology Filter MeasureTheory
open scoped ENNReal NNReal
open DefinitionOneSobolev.FixedPhasePeterssonCoordinates
open DefinitionOneSobolev.FixedPhaseGraphCompletion

open GammaTwoQuotientGeometry

/-- Explicit positive error used for the potential tail. -/
noncomputable def discriminantCuspEpsilon (N : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  1 / ((N : ℝ) + 1)

declarations.name: discriminantCuspEpsilon_pos
declarations.header:
theorem discriminantCuspEpsilon_pos (N : ℕ) :
    0 < discriminantCuspEpsilon N:=

declarations.name: discriminantCuspEpsilon_nonneg
declarations.header:
theorem discriminantCuspEpsilon_nonneg (N : ℕ) :
    0 ≤ discriminantCuspEpsilon N :=
  (discriminantCuspEpsilon_pos N).le

declarations.name: discriminantCuspEpsilon_tendsto_zero
declarations.header:
theorem discriminantCuspEpsilon_tendsto_zero :
    Filter.Tendsto discriminantCuspEpsilon Filter.atTop (nhds 0):=

declarations.name: one_le_discriminantLiteralCuspLevel
declarations.header:
theorem one_le_discriminantLiteralCuspLevel (N : ℕ) :
    1 ≤ discriminantLiteralCuspLevel N :=
  (Classical.choose_spec
    (potential_quotientOutside_threeCuspTruncationImage
      (discriminantCuspEpsilon_pos N))).1

/-- The selected level has the promised uniform pointwise potential tail on
the actual quotient complement. -/

declarations.name: potential_le_discriminantCuspEpsilon_outside_literalStage
declarations.header:
theorem potential_le_discriminantCuspEpsilon_outside_literalStage
    (N : ℕ) (q : GammaTwoQuotient)
    (hq : q ∉ gammaTwoQuotientMk ''
      gammaTwoThreeCuspTruncation (discriminantLiteralCuspLevel N)) :
    potential q ≤ discriminantCuspEpsilon N :=
  (Classical.choose_spec
    (potential_quotientOutside_threeCuspTruncationImage
      (discriminantCuspEpsilon_pos N))).2 q hq

section HardStageFactorization

variable {E : Type*}
variable [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℂ E]

/-- A compact hard-stage restriction remains compact after the bounded
potential pairing into the graph anti-dual. -/

declarations.name: hardStagePotentialFactor_isCompact
declarations.header:
theorem hardStagePotentialFactor_isCompact
    (n : ℤ)
    (stageRestriction : GraphSobolevCompletion n →L[ℂ] E)
    (stagePotentialPairing :
      E →L[ℂ] StrongAntiDual (GraphSobolevCompletion n))
    (hStage : IsCompactOperator stageRestriction) :
    IsCompactOperator (stagePotentialPairing.comp stageRestriction) :=
  hStage.clm_comp stagePotentialPairing

/-- Exact operator-norm endpoint for literal hard truncations.  The
approximants are not abstract compact certificates: each one is displayed as
the composition of a hard-stage restriction with a bounded potential pairing.
The quantitative bound is matched to the actual discriminant cusp scale
chosen above. -/

declarations.name: graphPotentialOperator_isCompact_of_literalStageFactorization
declarations.header:
theorem graphPotentialOperator_isCompact_of_literalStageFactorization

    (stageRestriction : ℕ → GraphSobolevCompletion n →L[ℂ] E)

      E →L[ℂ] StrongAntiDual (GraphSobolevCompletion n))
    (hStage : ∀ N, IsCompactOperator (stageRestriction N))
    (hTail : ∀ N,
      ‖(stagePotentialPairing N).comp (stageRestriction N) -
          graphPotentialOperator n‖ ≤ discriminantCuspEpsilon N) :
    IsCompactOperator (graphPotentialOperator n):=

/-- Lax--Milgram solution of one real shifted form equation. -/
noncomputable def embeddedFormResolventSolution
    (J : V →L[ℂ] H) (B : ContinuousSesquilinearForm V)
    (c α : ℝ)
    (hCoercive : ComplexCoerciveWith α (embeddedShiftedForm J B c))
    (y : H) : V :=
  solveWith α (embeddedShiftedForm J B c) hCoercive
    (embeddedAntiDual J y)

declarations.name: embeddedFormResolventSolution_spec
declarations.header:
theorem embeddedFormResolventSolution_spec
    (J : V →L[ℂ] H) (B : ContinuousSesquilinearForm V)
    (c α : ℝ)
    (hCoercive : ComplexCoerciveWith α (embeddedShiftedForm J B c))
    (y : H) (v : V) :
    embeddedShiftedForm J B c
        (embeddedFormResolventSolution J B c α hCoercive y) v =
      inner ℂ (J v) y:=

declarations.name: embeddedFormResolventSolution_mem_associatedGraph
declarations.header:
theorem embeddedFormResolventSolution_mem_associatedGraph
    (J : V →L[ℂ] H) (B : ContinuousSesquilinearForm V)
    (c α : ℝ)
    (hCoercive : ComplexCoerciveWith α (embeddedShiftedForm J B c))
    (y : H) :
    let u := embeddedFormResolventSolution J B c α hCoercive y
    (J u, y - (c : ℂ) • J u) ∈ associatedFormGraph J B:=

declarations.name: associatedFormOperator_realShift_surjective
declarations.header:
theorem associatedFormOperator_realShift_surjective
    (J : V →L[ℂ] H) (B : ContinuousSesquilinearForm V)
    (hJinj : Function.Injective J) (hJdense : DenseRange J)
    (c α : ℝ)

/-!
## P5.3: literal fixed-stage restriction on the physical carrier

The Rellich map must be the restriction of the *actual Euclidean Petersson
representative* to the genuine three-cusp stage.  It is not an abstract map
whose compactness is stored in a field.  This section constructs that map
directly with Mathlib's `LpToLpRestrictCLM` and records its representative,
linearity, and sharp contraction estimate.  The target measure is literally

`(volume.comap UpperHalfPlane.coe).restrict carrier | F_Y`.

Thus later Fourier charts have a fixed, checkable source and target.
-/

namespace Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev
namespace P5PhysicalHardStageRestriction

open Set Function Topology Filter MeasureTheory
open scoped ENNReal NNReal
open DefinitionOneSobolev
open DefinitionOneSobolev.FixedPhasePeterssonCoordinates
open DefinitionOneSobolev.FixedPhaseGraphCompletion
open GammaTwoQuotientGeometry
open FixedPhaseClosedOperators
open PhysicalLocalL2

/-- Euclidean carrier measure restricted to the literal three-cusp stage.
The repeated restriction is intentional: it makes the carrier and the
height truncation visible in the type. -/
noncomputable abbrev literalStageMeasure (Y : ℝ) : Measure ℍ :=
  chosenEuclideanCarrierMeasure.restrict
    (gammaTwoThreeCuspTruncation Y)

/-- Actual scalar `L2` space on one literal cusp-height stage. -/
noncomputable abbrev LiteralStageL2 (Y : ℝ) :=
  MeasureTheory.Lp ℂ 2 (literalStageMeasure Y)

/-- Restriction of the concrete Petersson representative to a literal stage. -/
noncomputable def peterssonLiteralStageRestriction (Y : ℝ) (n : ℤ) :
    OrbitPeterssonHilbert n →L[ℂ] LiteralStageL2 Y :=
  (MeasureTheory.LpToLpRestrictCLM ℍ ℂ ℂ
    chosenEuclideanCarrierMeasure 2
    (gammaTwoThreeCuspTruncation Y)).comp
      (orbitPeterssonEuclideanEmbedding n)

/-- The genuine graph-to-stage map.  Only the base Petersson coordinate is
restricted; the two derivative coordinates remain available in the source
norm and will control its Fourier tail. -/
noncomputable def graphLiteralStageRestriction (Y : ℝ) (n : ℤ) :
    GraphSobolevCompletion n →L[ℂ] LiteralStageL2 Y :=
  (peterssonLiteralStageRestriction Y n).comp (baseExtension n)

@[simp]

declarations.header:

    (x : GraphSobolevCompletion n) :
    graphLiteralStageRestriction Y n x =
      MeasureTheory.LpToLpRestrictCLM ℍ ℂ ℂ
        chosenEuclideanCarrierMeasure 2
        (gammaTwoThreeCuspTruncation Y)
        (orbitPeterssonEuclideanEmbedding n (baseExtension n x)) :=
  rfl

/-!
## P5.4: quantitative Fourier tails (operator-norm, not pointwise)

Strong convergence of Fourier partial sums on each fixed `L2` vector is not
Rellich compactness.  What is required is a bound uniform on the graph unit
ball.  The following small lemmas turn the exact estimate produced by the two
weak physical derivatives into operator-norm convergence.  They are kept
separate so a later chart proof cannot accidentally substitute pointwise
Parseval convergence for the uniform tail estimate.
-/

namespace Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev
namespace P5LocalFourierRellich

open Function Set Topology Filter MeasureTheory

section QuantitativeTail

variable {H : Type*}
variable [NormedAddCommGroup H] [InnerProductSpace ℂ H]

/-- Uniform Fourier remainder estimate on a bounded map. -/
def HasQuantitativeFiniteModeTail
    (modes : ℕ → Finset (Fin 2 → ℤ))
    (T : H →L[ℂ] TwoTorusL2) (delta : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  (∀ N, 0 ≤ delta N) ∧
    ∀ N x,
      ‖finiteModeLocalization twoTorusFourierBasis (modes N) T x - T x‖ ≤
        delta N * ‖x‖

declarations.name: opNorm_sub_le_of_quantitativeFiniteModeTail
declarations.header:
theorem opNorm_sub_le_of_quantitativeFiniteModeTail
    (modes : ℕ → Finset (Fin 2 → ℤ))
    (T : H →L[ℂ] TwoTorusL2) (delta : ℕ → ℝ)
    (h : HasQuantitativeFiniteModeTail modes T delta) (N : ℕ) :
    ‖finiteModeLocalization twoTorusFourierBasis (modes N) T - T‖ ≤
      delta N:=

declarations.name: hasVanishingFiniteModeTail_of_quantitative
declarations.header:
theorem hasVanishingFiniteModeTail_of_quantitative
    (modes : ℕ → Finset (Fin 2 → ℤ))
    (T : H →L[ℂ] TwoTorusL2) (delta : ℕ → ℝ)
    (h : HasQuantitativeFiniteModeTail modes T delta)
    (hdelta : Filter.Tendsto delta Filter.atTop (nhds 0)) :
    HasVanishingFiniteModeTail twoTorusFourierBasis modes T:=

declarations.name: twoTorus_isCompactOperator_of_quantitativeTail
declarations.header:
theorem twoTorus_isCompactOperator_of_quantitativeTail
    (modes : ℕ → Finset (Fin 2 → ℤ))
    (T : H →L[ℂ] TwoTorusL2) (delta : ℕ → ℝ)
    (h : HasQuantitativeFiniteModeTail modes T delta)
    (hdelta : Filter.Tendsto delta Filter.atTop (nhds 0)) :
    IsCompactOperator T :=
  twoTorus_isCompactOperator_of_fourierTail modes T
    (hasVanishingFiniteModeTail_of_quantitative modes T delta h hdelta)

/-- The canonical `C/(N+1)` error scale. -/
noncomputable def reciprocalFourierTail (C : ℝ) (N : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  C / ((N : ℝ) + 1)

declarations.header:
theorem reciprocalFourierTail_nonneg {C : ℝ} (hC : 0 ≤ C) (N : ℕ) :
    0 ≤ reciprocalFourierTail C N:=

declarations.header:

    (modes : ℕ → Finset (Fin 2 → ℤ))
    (T : H →L[ℂ] TwoTorusL2) (C : ℝ) (hC : 0 ≤ C)
    (hTail : ∀ N x,
      ‖finiteModeLocalization twoTorusFourierBasis (modes N) T x - T x‖ ≤
        reciprocalFourierTail C N * ‖x‖) :
    IsCompactOperator T:=

/-!
## P11. Honest spectral/Kuznetsov boundary

The functional-analytic package does not manufacture a half-integral
Kuznetsov formula, Eisenstein normalization, scattering Plancherel theorem,
or a multiplier-dependent Kloosterman estimate. None is currently available
in Mathlib at the normalization used here. This section formalizes only the
exact final logical reduction: valid lower and upper estimates must have an
actual crossover index. Every premise stays visible and no inhabitant for the
manuscript's proposed arithmetic estimates is constructed.
-/

namespace Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.P11ConditionalReduction

open Set

/-- Complete numerical input needed at the final comparison step. -/
def ExactLowerUpperCrossoverInput
    (S lower upper : ℕ → ℝ) (I : Set ℕ) : Prop :=
  (∀ m ∈ I, lower m ≤ S m) ∧
    (∀ m, |S m| ≤ upper m) ∧
      ∃ m ∈ I, upper m < lower m

/-- With all three premises proved for one normalization and one test family,
the contradiction is immediate. -/

declarations.name: false_of_exactLowerUpperCrossoverInput
declarations.header:
theorem false_of_exactLowerUpperCrossoverInput
    {S lower upper : ℕ → ℝ} {I : Set ℕ}
    (h : ExactLowerUpperCrossoverInput S lower upper I) : False :=
  contradiction_of_lower_upper_cross h.1 h.2.1 h.2.2

/-- Quantitative lower activity explicitly contains an index-independent
positive constant. -/
def HasUniformLowerActivity
    (mass : ℕ → ℝ) (I : Set ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∃ δ : ℝ, 0 < δ ∧ ∀ m ∈ I, δ ≤ mass m

/-- Uniform lower activity implies pointwise nonnegativity on selected
indices. The converse is deliberately absent and is refuted in P10. -/

declarations.name: nonneg_on_of_hasUniformLowerActivity
declarations.header:
theorem nonneg_on_of_hasUniformLowerActivity
    {mass : ℕ → ℝ} {I : Set ℕ}
    (h : HasUniformLowerActivity mass I) :
    ∀ m ∈ I, 0 ≤ mass m:=

declarations.name: fixedLower_polynomialUpper_has_no_forced_contradiction
declarations.header:
theorem fixedLower_polynomialUpper_has_no_forced_contradiction
    (δ : ℝ) (hδ : 0 < δ) :
    ∃ S : ℕ → ℝ,
      (∀ m, δ ≤ S m) ∧
        (∀ m, |S m| ≤ δ + (m : ℝ)) :=
  fixed_lower_compatible_with_polynomial_upper δ hδ

end Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.P11ConditionalReduction

/-!
### P6 strong/weak bridge on the actual fixed-phase smooth core

This section identifies the already constructed three-coordinate weak
Schrodinger form with one literal second-order differential expression on the
genuine automorphic smooth core.  The two first-order coordinates are moved
off the test section by the unconditional quotient Green identities, and the
two exact raising/lowering factorizations retain their full weight-dependent

an actual endomorphism of the smooth fixed-phase core.

No elliptic-regularity converse is asserted for an arbitrary graph-completion
vector.  The converse below has the mathematically precise hypothesis that the
weak solution is represented by an element of the actual smooth core; on that

    strongPrincipalCore n u =
      u - Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.HalfWeightDifferentialOperators.InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore.lowerFromSucc n
          (Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.HalfWeightDifferentialOperators.InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore.raise n u) -
        Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.HalfWeightDifferentialOperators.InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore.raiseFromPred n
          (Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.HalfWeightDifferentialOperators.InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore.lower n u) :=
  rfl

/-- Both exact factorization identities combine to the full (not averaged)
second-order differential expression.  In particular the constant is
`1 + physicalExponent`, not an untracked generic shift. -/

declarations.name: strongPrincipalCore_apply_pointwise
declarations.header:
theorem strongPrincipalCore_apply_pointwise (n : ℤ)
    (u : Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.HalfWeightDifferentialOperators.InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore n) (z : ℍ) :
    ((strongPrincipalCore n u : Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.HalfWeightDifferentialOperators.InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore n) :
        SmoothQuotientCompactFunction) z =
      ((1 : ℂ) + physicalExponent (paperOrbitExponent n)) *
          (u : SmoothQuotientCompactFunction) z +
        2 * laplaceRaw (paperOrbitExponent n)
          (u : SmoothQuotientCompactFunction) z:=

declarations.name: strongSchrodingerCore_apply
declarations.header:
theorem strongSchrodingerCore_apply (n : ℤ) (t : ℝ)
    (u : Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.HalfWeightDifferentialOperators.InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore n) :
    strongSchrodingerCore n t u =
      strongPrincipalCore n u -
        (t : ℂ) • potentialMultiplicationCore n u :=
  rfl

/-- The raw differential expression, displayed independently of the bundled
core endomorphism. -/
noncomputable def strongSchrodingerDifferentialExpression
    (n : ℤ) (t : ℝ) (u : Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.HalfWeightDifferentialOperators.InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore n) (z : ℍ) : ℂ :=
  ((1 : ℂ) + physicalExponent (paperOrbitExponent n)) *
      (u : SmoothQuotientCompactFunction) z +
    2 * laplaceRaw (paperOrbitExponent n)
      (u : SmoothQuotientCompactFunction) z -
    (t : ℂ) * (upstairsPotential z : ℂ) *
      (u : SmoothQuotientCompactFunction) z

/-- The bundled strong core operator is pointwise exactly the corrected
Laplacian expression plus the explicit scalar potential. -/

declarations.name: strongSchrodingerCore_apply_pointwise
declarations.header:
theorem strongSchrodingerCore_apply_pointwise (n : ℤ) (t : ℝ)
    (u : Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.HalfWeightDifferentialOperators.InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore n) (z : ℍ) :
    ((strongSchrodingerCore n t u : Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.HalfWeightDifferentialOperators.InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore n) :
        SmoothQuotientCompactFunction) z =
      strongSchrodingerDifferentialExpression n t u z:=

    minimalStrongSchrodinger n t ≤ modularAssociatedOperator n t:=

declarations.name: minimalStrongSchrodinger_eq_associated_domRestrict
declarations.header:
theorem minimalStrongSchrodinger_eq_associated_domRestrict
    (n : ℤ) (t : ℝ) :
    minimalStrongSchrodinger n t =
      (modularAssociatedOperator n t).domRestrict
        (minimalStrongSchrodinger n t).domain :=
  eq_domRestrict_of_le
    (minimalStrongSchrodinger_le_modularAssociatedOperator n t)

/-- The minimal strong operator is closable because it has the already-proved
closed self-adjoint form realization as an extension. -/

declarations.name: minimalStrongSchrodinger_isClosable
declarations.header:
theorem minimalStrongSchrodinger_isClosable (n : ℤ) (t : ℝ) :
    (minimalStrongSchrodinger n t).IsClosable :=
  (modularAssociatedOperator_isClosed n t).isClosable.leIsClosable
    (minimalStrongSchrodinger_le_modularAssociatedOperator n t)

/-- Its canonical graph closure remains inside the self-adjoint realization. -/

declarations.name: minimalStrongSchrodinger_closure_le_modularAssociatedOperator
declarations.header:
theorem minimalStrongSchrodinger_closure_le_modularAssociatedOperator
    (n : ℤ) (t : ℝ) :
    (minimalStrongSchrodinger n t).closure ≤
      modularAssociatedOperator n t:=

declarations.name: minimalStrongSchrodinger_closure_isClosed
declarations.header:
theorem minimalStrongSchrodinger_closure_isClosed (n : ℤ) (t : ℝ) :
    (minimalStrongSchrodinger n t).closure.IsClosed :=
  (minimalStrongSchrodinger_isClosable n t).closure_isClosed

/-! ### The maximal distributional operator -/

/-- The maximal Hilbert-space realization of the same literal core
differential expression is its Mathlib adjoint. -/
noncomputable def maximalStrongSchrodinger (n : ℤ) (t : ℝ) :
    OrbitPeterssonHilbert n →ₗ.[ℂ] OrbitPeterssonHilbert n :=
  (minimalStrongSchrodinger n t)†

/-- The maximal realization is closed by the standard Hilbert adjoint API. -/

declarations.name: maximalStrongSchrodinger_isClosed
declarations.header:
theorem maximalStrongSchrodinger_isClosed (n : ℤ) (t : ℝ) :
    (maximalStrongSchrodinger n t).IsClosed:=

theorem maximalStrongSchrodinger_dense_domain (n : ℤ) (t : ℝ) :

declarations.header:

    S.IsFormalAdjoint A:=

  formalAdjoint_extension_of_le
    (minimalStrongSchrodinger_le_modularAssociatedOperator n t)
    (modularAssociatedOperator_isFormalAdjoint n t)

/-- Conjugate formal-adjoint orientation, recorded separately because this is
the one used when testing a maximal-domain vector by a smooth core vector. -/

declarations.name: modularAssociatedOperator_isFormalAdjoint_minimalStrong
declarations.header:
theorem modularAssociatedOperator_isFormalAdjoint_minimalStrong
    (n : ℤ) (t : ℝ) :
    (modularAssociatedOperator n t).IsFormalAdjoint

  (minimalStrongSchrodinger_isFormalAdjoint_associated n t).symm

/-- Minimal symmetry gives the first minimal-to-maximal inclusion. -/

declarations.name: minimalStrongSchrodinger_le_maximalStrongSchrodinger
declarations.header:
theorem minimalStrongSchrodinger_le_maximalStrongSchrodinger
    (n : ℤ) (t : ℝ) :

declarations.header:
theorem modularAssociatedOperator_le_maximalStrongSchrodinger
    (n : ℤ) (t : ℝ) :
    modularAssociatedOperator n t ≤ maximalStrongSchrodinger n t:=

declarations.name: maximalStrongSchrodinger_adjoint_eq_minimalClosure
declarations.header:
theorem maximalStrongSchrodinger_adjoint_eq_minimalClosure
    (n : ℤ) (t : ℝ) :
    (maximalStrongSchrodinger n t)† =
      (minimalStrongSchrodinger n t).closure:=

declarations.name: minimalStrongSchrodinger_closure_le_maximalStrongSchrodinger
declarations.header:
theorem minimalStrongSchrodinger_closure_le_maximalStrongSchrodinger
    (n : ℤ) (t : ℝ) :
    (minimalStrongSchrodinger n t).closure ≤
      maximalStrongSchrodinger n t :=
  (minimalStrongSchrodinger_closure_le_modularAssociatedOperator n t).trans
    (modularAssociatedOperator_le_maximalStrongSchrodinger n t)

/-- The entire honest minimal/closed-form/maximal chain. -/

declarations.name: minimal_closure_associated_maximal_chain
declarations.header:
theorem minimal_closure_associated_maximal_chain
    (n : ℤ) (t : ℝ) :
    minimalStrongSchrodinger n t ≤
        (minimalStrongSchrodinger n t).closure ∧
      (minimalStrongSchrodinger n t).closure ≤
        modularAssociatedOperator n t ∧
      modularAssociatedOperator n t ≤
        maximalStrongSchrodinger n t :=
  ⟨(minimalStrongSchrodinger n t).le_closure,
    minimalStrongSchrodinger_closure_le_modularAssociatedOperator n t,
    modularAssociatedOperator_le_maximalStrongSchrodinger n t⟩

/-! ### Exact maximal weak graph identity -/

/-- Membership in the maximal graph is exactly the distributional pairing
identity against every vector in the literal minimal domain. -/

declarations.name: mem_maximalStrongSchrodinger_graph_iff_domain_tests
declarations.header:
theorem mem_maximalStrongSchrodinger_graph_iff_domain_tests
    (n : ℤ) (t : ℝ) (x f : OrbitPeterssonHilbert n) :
    (x, f) ∈ (maximalStrongSchrodinger n t).graph ↔
      ∀ y : (minimalStrongSchrodinger n t).domain,
        inner ℂ (minimalStrongSchrodinger n t y) x =
          inner ℂ (y : OrbitPeterssonHilbert n) f:=

declarations.name: mem_maximalStrongSchrodinger_graph_iff_core_tests
declarations.header:
theorem mem_maximalStrongSchrodinger_graph_iff_core_tests
    (n : ℤ) (t : ℝ) (x f : OrbitPeterssonHilbert n) :
    (x, f) ∈ (maximalStrongSchrodinger n t).graph ↔
      ∀ u : Mock2FA.PaperCorrections.AutomorphicSobolev.HalfWeightDifferentialOperators.InverseEtaFixedPhaseCore n,
        inner ℂ (l2Coordinate n (strongSchrodingerCore n t u)) x =
          inner ℂ (l2Coordinate n u) f:=

declarations.name: smoothCoreIsOperatorCore_iff_closure_eq_associated
declarations.header:
